direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is dependent on the film's four distinct styles, where the Barney parody style is very much entertaining as it pokes fun at evil Barney conspiracies and creepypastas, while the real world is basic, predictable, and incredibly surface level; the direction on a microscale is surprisingly pretty good, especially because the director gets a lot out of the child actors and the voice talent, making them a highlight while Cristin Milioti carries her scenes despite generic react-to-horror material; the storytelling is incredibly basic, dragging out a concept that legitimately didn't need to be a movie as it could have just been a YouTube creepypasta; the tension is built fine in a basic way, doing a decent job but relying heavily on common horror tropes

performance.comments: Shows her talent as an actress as she does best she can to make her character interesting and sympathetic despite limited material
The real star of the show as she shows a pretty good range of emotions for a child actress and does her best to carry her scenes, especially in the end
Plays a very Topher Grace character as I've definitely seen him play this character multiple times
The perfect fit for the role, completely encapsulating the fake-nice attitude and secret evil nature of Buddy with his natural comedic charm

cast.comments: Highlighted by outstanding performances from the child actors, showing good talent and good direction of actors, helping the cast have pretty good chemistry as a whole

story.comments: The concept is a funny idea, 20 years ago, poking fun at early 2000s evil Barney conspiracies and creepypastas, but it is incredibly surface level and legitimately didn't need to be stretched out into a full movie; the plot structure is respectable for not being purely linear, starting with separate A and B plots that gradually converge into one, though it suffers from dragging and stretching time with unnecessarily long scenes; character writing is very basic and surface level, delivering exactly what you expect with a concerned mother, a fearful child who learns to overcome her fears, and typical personified characters in a Barney-style world

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is incredibly basic and predictable, poking fun at the kid-friendly nature of Barney type shows; the humor is fun and entertaining because of how silly the idea is, made even more enjoyable with Keegan-Michael Key being naturally funny as the evil guy; the symbolism is non-existent, serving merely as a surface-level, generic horror template with zero underlying meaning; the foreshadowing is overt and relies on heavy horror cliches, making the film incredibly predictable as you know exactly what is going to happen

score.comments: Used mostly to complete the world we are in, either horror in the horror elements or friendly in the barney style world

soundtrack.comments: Very much like kids songs making fun of Barney and emulating that style

cinematography.comments: Varies across four distinct styles; the Barney parody effectively emulates 90s kids television, the outside world feels cheap like a YouTube web series, the real world is generic horror, and the climax is uniquely shot in a third-person style

editing.comments: Complements each of the four styles well (using circular fades for the 90s TV parody), but hindered by unnecessarily long cuts and sequences that make the movie drag

sound.comments: Delivers exactly what you expect, blending standard horror movie sounds with the cheerful audio of a Barney parody

visual_effects.comments: Intentionally low budget and over the top to emulate cheap 90s/00s television, adding to the low-budget slasher nature of the movie

production_design.comments: Strongest in the Barney parody world and cheap-looking outside world, effectively capturing 90s kids television vibes while feeling unoriginal by relying on recent Backrooms horror trends

makeup.comments: Does the job of showing blood and gore naturally for a slasher movie

costumes.comments: Mostly for the mascot-style outfits that perfectly emulate the Barney aesthetic

review.pacing: Incredibly slow, fluffing out many scenes and storylines with unnecessarily long sequences where trimming 10-15 minutes could have tightened the movie significantly
review.climax: Entertaining in content, but feels incredibly long, while remaining completely predictable
review.tone: Varies across the four styles of the movie: the nostalgic yet eerie aesthetic of late 90s/early 2000s children's television brings the creepypasta to life; the outside world presents cheap, YouTube-style horror; the real world is generic horror; and the climax emulates the Backrooms style of modern creepypasta, but in a derivative way
review.final_notes: My enjoyment of this movie is very similar to Backrooms, as the creepypasta aspects are what make the movie, but the story they try to build alongside it is just very generic and basic
review.overall: Overall, 'Buddy' very much is just a movie because while I can relate to the story considering the early 2000s 'Barney is evil' creepypasta is something I grew up with, I can also admit that I haven't cared about that idea in almost 20 years; while Buddy does a pretty good job at bringing the 'Barney is Evil' creepypasta to life and is carried by entertaining performances by Cristin Milioti, Keegan-Michael Key, and the child actors, the movie plays like a surface-level slasher film that feels both predictable and like it is dragging for time, making me feel like this honestly could have been a 40-minute creepypasta on YouTube
